text:
Marathon Petroleum stock jumped 4.8% today as oil prices spiked on geopolitical tension: Iran escalated tanker attacks on shipping in the Gulf, and the Trump administration simultaneously announced new sanctions on Iran's "shadow fleet" and discussed potential military operations. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude oil prices typically improve profitability on the refining side—they can sell finished products like gasoline and diesel at premium prices when oil costs surge. Refineries are already running at 92.7% capacity, so the company is well-positioned to capitalize on the price premium.

The two-week rally (up 18.5%) reflects a broader tightening in global oil markets: world crude has climbed sharply, diesel prices are becoming a political flashpoint ahead of midterm elections, and storage levels for both crude and refined products remain relatively tight. This combination of supply concerns and strong demand keeps fuel prices elevated, which works in a large refiner's favor.
